tema: Examines which prior and concurrent factors in infectious mononucleosis predict the development of severe ME/CFS at 6 months.
diseno: Prospective cohort of 4501 university students, of whom 238 developed mononucleosis; analysis of 48 with ME/CFS at 6 months (30 ME/CFS and 18 severe) and 58 recovered controls; questionnaires, physical examination, mononucleosis severity and cytokines before and during infection; ROC curves.
hallazgos: Students with severe gastrointestinal symptoms (abdominal pain, bloating, irritable bowel) and abnormally low levels of IL-13 and/or IL-5 before becoming ill, and severe gastrointestinal symptoms during mononucleosis, had almost an 80% probability of severe ME/CFS at 6 months.
conclusion: Gastrointestinal distress, autonomic symptoms and several immune markers could be involved in the development of severe ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the abstract) are consistent; the conclusions text repeats that of the abstract followed by the introduction, with no independent information.

tema: Proposes that vitamin D3 deficiency and cellular stress responses explain the progression from mild-moderate chronic fatigue to severe CFS/ME.
diseno: Theoretical article based on literature on cellular stress responses and the effects of vitamin D3. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Cellular stress responses are closely linked to effects of vitamin D3 on metabolism, energy, redox balance and defence against pathogens; personality traits, indoor activities, latitude and climate would predispose to deficiency, and in severe stages there appears to be resistance to mere replacement.
conclusion: Vitamin D deficiency should be considered a causal and aggravating factor in diseases with chronic fatigue; the author proposes early diagnosis, personalized high doses and avoiding stressors, although he calls for clinical observation to confirm reversibility.
triangulacion: There are no keywords. Abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions go further with dose recommendations and specific measures not supported by own data.

tema: Argues that ischaemia-reperfusion injury underlies part of the pathology of chronic relapsing diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, long COVID and ME/CFS.
hallazgos: Ischaemia could be initiated by capillary blockage with amyloid fibrin microclots at the start of exercise, and reperfusion at the end; evidence of oxidative stress, hyperinflammation, mast cell activation and marker metabolites is reviewed, which would explain dyspnoea, fatigue and PEM.
conclusion: If the analysis is correct, there would be potential therapeutic benefit with antioxidants, anti-inflammatories, iron chelators and safe fibrinolytics or anticoagulants.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions (with noise from figure caption and download text) make the therapeutic implications conditional on the analysis being correct. The main focus is long COVID rather than ME/CFS.

tema: Philosophical reply to Sharpe and Greco criticizing the 'illness without disease' approach and its use of Whitehead's bifurcation of nature.
diseno: Opinion article in philosophy of medicine; no empirical data.
hallazgos: Maintains that experience is no longer considered secondary to bodily states and that medical explanations must be evaluated before philosophical ones; the NIH, IOM and US health bodies consider ME/CFS a biomedical disease.
conclusion: It is no longer sustainable or safe to ignore the possibility of disease in ME/CFS or to recommend that clinicians do so; the conceptual foundations must be reconsidered.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the conclusions text is just a list of references (noise), with no contribution for triangulation.

tema: Correspondence in Nature analysing nominations for the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (1901-1966), together with other unrelated letters.
diseno: Analysis of hundreds of public nomination letters; detailed methods not stated.
hallazgos: Some nominations highlight lifetime achievements and others discoveries that open new areas of research (e.g., Lister and Huggins).
triangulacion: Only the opening text is available, without keywords or conclusions; the document does not deal with ME/CFS and appears to have been included in the collection by mistake.

tema: Synthesizes the multifactorial origins of ME/CFS into a cohesive model of its biology.
diseno: Integrative narrative review. No sample stated.
hallazgos: ME/CFS would arise from genetic vulnerabilities and environmental triggers, above all viral infections, which lead to immune dysregulation, chronic inflammation, gut dysbiosis and metabolic alterations; in addition, it lacks standardized diagnostic criteria and effective treatments.
conclusion: The model opens new avenues of research and therapy and demands a holistic approach to diagnosis, research and treatment, with patient participation.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the discussion text contains almost only contributions and funding, apart from a mention of including patient input in future research.

tema: Opinion article on the role of immunity and inflammation in ME/CFS and post-COVID syndrome and its therapeutic implications.
diseno: Opinion article that contrasts the author's clinical experience with the literature and includes preliminary results from a prospective two-centre open-label trial; sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Oral nutraceuticals, sodium dichloroacetate and meldonium are proposed, along with infusions of magnesium, multivitamins, glutathione, tranexamic acid and cultured stem cells; preliminary data suggest that more than four in five patients improve with combined therapy.
conclusion: There is no causal treatment; treating the altered immunity and chronic inflammation remains the best option, biologics and JAK inhibitors deserve trials, and the priority is to reduce the prevalence of post-COVID with early nirmatrelvir and vaccination.
triangulacion: There are no keywords. Abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions add prevention through nirmatrelvir and vaccination, and the therapeutic results come from a preliminary open-label trial without a control group.

tema: Examines static and dynamic functional connectivity during a fatiguing cognitive task in CFS using arterial spin labelling (ASL) fMRI.
diseno: ASL fMRI in 19 CFS patients and 15 healthy controls during a fatiguing cognitive task; regions selected a priori.
hallazgos: Controls showed a greater increase in static insula-temporo-occipital region and precuneus-thalamus/striatum connectivity; inferior frontal gyrus connectivity fell in controls and rose in CFS. Patients had lower dynamic hippocampus-superior parietal lobe connectivity, and both measures correlated with induced fatigue.
conclusion: Static and dynamic connectivity alterations could underlie task-induced fatigue; whether treatments normalize them should be studied.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent on dynamic connectivity, ASL and insula; the conclusions focus on the dynamic connectivity of memory and attention regions.
